modules.title: Trend rules, breakouts, and turnover
modules.subtitle: Specify an executable trend rule with entry, exit, warm-up, and turnover controls.
modules.objective: Specify an executable trend rule with entry, exit, warm-up, and turnover controls.
modules.reading: Unit 2 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A rule must define the information window precisely. For a breakout observed at today's completed close, compare that close with an earlier high window that excludes today. Including today's high changes the question and can make a strict close-above-high test impossible. A moving-average rule instead compares levels computed from a declared window.

Use separate entry and exit thresholds when a small fluctuation would otherwise churn the portfolio. This hysteresis is a design choice with a trade-off: less turnover can delay an exit. Do not select the band after inspecting the final evaluation period.

$$
\text{Entry threshold}=\max(H_{t-L},\ldots,H_{t-1})(1+b)
$$

## A worked example

Earlier highs are 100, 102, and 101. A completed close of 103 exceeds the prior maximum of 102. Under an illustrative rule requiring a 0.5% breakout, the entry threshold is 102.51, so the signal qualifies. A 1.5% band would require 103.53 and would not qualify. Execution occurs on a later eligible event, whose price need not equal 103.

A backtest earns 1.2% gross while turning the portfolio over six one-way notional equivalents. At 15 bps per equivalent, estimated trading costs are 0.9%, leaving 0.3% before other omitted costs.

## Implementation and review

Build a fixture for a flat market, a gap, a missing close, and a split-adjustment mismatch. Evaluate a small preregistered parameter grid on training and validation windows, then freeze it. Report return, drawdown, time in market, turnover, and sensitivity to costs. A trend indicator is a descriptive transformation; the ability to compute it does not establish an economic edge.

modules.title: Mean reversion and pairs hypotheses
modules.subtitle: Distinguish a normalized deviation from evidence of reversion and account for both legs of a spread.
modules.objective: Distinguish a normalized deviation from evidence of reversion and account for both legs of a spread.
modules.reading: Unit 2 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A z-score describes deviation relative to an estimated mean and scale. It is not a guarantee that price will return to a historical level. Structural changes can move both the mean and variance. Specify the estimation window, fit the relationship using past data, and explain why a temporary displacement might close.

For pairs, define a spread such as A minus beta times B. Correlation of returns does not prove that this price spread is stationary. A fitted hedge ratio, a stationarity diagnostic, and an economic relationship answer different questions. Check sensitivity to sample choice and corporate changes before treating a spread as tradable.

$$
z_t=(s_t-\mu_{train})/\sigma_{train}
$$

## A worked example

A spread of 14 has a training mean of 10 and standard deviation 2, giving a z-score of 2. Harbor's paper research rule considers selling the spread above 1.5. That requires short A and long beta units of B under the stated sign convention; the current in-app long/cash sandbox cannot express both legs.

If the planned legs are $10,000 long and $10,000 short, net dollar exposure is zero but gross exposure is $20,000. Fees, stock borrow, asymmetric fills, beta mismatch, and abrupt divergence can still produce a loss.

## Implementation and review

Keep pairs work as a research worksheet unless the execution engine explicitly supports borrow availability, short margin, and two-leg state. Test a one-leg fill, a borrow recall, and a spread that never reverts. Define an exit based on elapsed time or invalidated evidence as well as the signal. Zero estimated net exposure must never bypass gross and concentration limits.

print("Gross exposure:", abs(10000) + abs(-10000))

# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.

modules.objective: Evaluate a frozen trading rule using a declared information cutoff, execution delay, benchmark, and cost model.
modules.reading: Unit 2 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Separate signal time, order time, and fill time. A strategy computed from a completed closing bar cannot assume it entered earlier at that bar's open. An OHLC bar also does not reveal whether its high preceded its low. Any intrabar stop or limit convention is an assumption that needs documentation.

Keep research selection distinct from final evaluation. Changing a window after seeing the holdout makes that period part of development. Record every tried variant, fit preprocessing on training data, and keep an untouched later segment for the final frozen rule. Corporate actions, delistings, and availability timestamps belong in the data audit.

$$
\Pi=q(P_{exit}-P_{entry})-f q(P_{entry}+P_{exit})
$$

## A worked example

Harbor signals at a close of 100 and buys 10 shares at the next open of 102. Later it sells at 104. At 5 bps commission on each notional, entry commission is $0.51 and exit commission $0.52. Net P&L is $18.97. Pretending entry occurred at the signal close would overstate the gross profit by $20.

If slippage is modeled in the fill price, do not subtract the same slippage again as a separate ledger fee. Compare with a passive position using the same timestamps, capital, and cost convention.

## Implementation and review

Review an order-by-order trace in addition to aggregate statistics. Report drawdown, turnover, exposure, number of independent decisions, and a cost stress. A smooth curve from few trades does not support a precise Sharpe claim. Use the sandbox to demonstrate timing and costs; use the offline project for event and ledger failure tests. Neither establishes a live execution advantage.

modules.title: Quotes, spread, and implementation shortfall
modules.subtitle: Measure an execution against a declared decision benchmark while distinguishing spread, impact, and delay.
modules.objective: Measure an execution against a declared decision benchmark while distinguishing spread, impact, and delay.
modules.reading: Unit 3 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A quote is an indication at a particular time, size, and venue. The midpoint is useful as a benchmark but is not necessarily executable. A marketable buy typically consumes offered liquidity; a resting limit may fail to fill or fill when the market moves against it. Better price and greater fill certainty are competing objectives.

Implementation shortfall compares execution with a decision benchmark, adjusted for trade direction. Explicit fees can be added separately. Spread, market impact, and delay are explanatory components whose estimates may overlap; avoid presenting a precise causal decomposition without the necessary data.

$$
IS_{bps}=10^4 d(P_{fill}/P_{decision}-1),\quad d\in\{+1,-1\}
$$

## A worked example

The bid is 99.90 and the ask 100.10, so the midpoint is 100 and the quoted spread is 20 bps. A buy filling at 100.12 costs 12 bps relative to that midpoint before commission. Half the quoted spread accounts for 10 bps in a simple interpretation; the extra 2 bps cannot be confidently called permanent impact from this single observation.

A sell at 99.88 also has 12 bps adverse shortfall under a direction-adjusted convention. Use consistent signs so a worse sell is not accidentally reported as a benefit.

## Implementation and review

Store the benchmark's source, timestamp, and size with each decision. Report fill rate and unfilled opportunity cost alongside the average cost of completed trades; measuring only successful fills can flatter passive strategies. Paper fills do not reproduce queue priority, hidden liquidity, or adverse selection. The course uses explicit toy assumptions that should be challenged before interpreting results.

modules.title: Order state machines and cancellation races
modules.subtitle: Handle acknowledgements, partial fills, cancellations, rejections, and ambiguous submissions without losing commitments.
modules.objective: Handle acknowledgements, partial fills, cancellations, rejections, and ambiguous submissions without losing commitments.
modules.reading: Unit 3 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Model submission, acknowledgement, partial fill, complete fill, cancellation, and rejection as explicit states with legal transitions. A timeout is an observation about communication, not necessarily an order state. Broker messages can arrive twice or out of order, so deduplicate by durable identity and reconcile cumulative quantities.

Separate an intent ID from an external order ID and a fill ID. One intent may have a documented cancel-and-replace sequence, while one order may have many fills. Track original quantity, cumulative filled quantity, remaining quantity, and cancellation status. Do not assume a cancellation acknowledgement erases earlier fills.

$$
q_{remaining}=q_{original}-\sum_i q_{fill,i}
$$

## A worked example

An order buys 100 shares. Forty fill, leaving 60. The bot requests cancellation, but 15 more fill before the cancellation completes. The ledger must contain 55 bought shares; the successful cancellation removes only the remaining 45. If the 15-share fill message is replayed, holdings remain 55.

If the broker reports cumulative filled quantity of 55, do not treat it as 55 additional shares after already booking 40. Distinguish incremental fill messages from cumulative order updates in the adapter contract.

## Implementation and review

Build a transition table and test every terminal state. Preserve unknown orders as risk commitments until reconciliation resolves them. Record rejected transitions for investigation instead of forcing state to match the latest message blindly. The offline lab demonstrates partial fills and idempotent fill records; a real asynchronous adapter additionally needs broker-specific cancel races and sequencing behavior.

modules.title: Execution schedules: TWAP, VWAP, and participation
modules.subtitle: Choose and evaluate a slicing policy with explicit urgency, liquidity, and completion constraints.
modules.objective: Choose and evaluate a slicing policy with explicit urgency, liquidity, and completion constraints.
modules.reading: Unit 3 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

TWAP distributes quantity over time; VWAP schedules against an estimated volume profile; a participation policy sizes child orders relative to observed or estimated market volume. Each needs a remaining-quantity cap, eligibility rules, and an end-of-window policy. Naming the algorithm does not define its actual fill mechanics.

Fast execution reduces waiting exposure but can consume expensive liquidity. Slow execution may reduce immediate pressure while risking price movement or an unfinished parent order. Models that optimize this trade-off rely on assumptions about volatility, impact, and constraints; there is no universally optimal schedule.

$$
q_{child}\leq\min(q_{remaining},\rho V_{eligible})
$$

## A worked example

A 1,000-share parent has four equal time buckets. TWAP requests 250 per bucket. A forecast volume profile of 10%, 20%, 40%, and 30% suggests VWAP child targets of 100, 200, 400, and 300. Under a 5% participation cap, a bucket with 4,000 shares of eligible volume permits at most 200 shares, even when the schedule asks for 400.

The remaining 200 cannot simply disappear from the report. The parent needs a documented carry-forward, cancellation, or urgency change, with risk approval. Do not use a bucket's eventual full volume for an order placed before that volume was known.

## Implementation and review

Simulate sparse volume, a missed bucket, a session ending early, and a late cancellation. Report both shortfall and completion percentage. A schedule should preserve parent quantity after partial fills and retries. Cap each child by remaining authorized quantity as well as participation; otherwise a catch-up rule can overfill the original decision.

parent = 1000
print("TWAP slice:", parent / 4)
profile = [0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.3]
for weight in profile:
    print("VWAP target:", parent * weight)
print("Participation cap:", 4000 * 0.05)

# This worksheet computes the case above. The price sandbox stays in cash.
# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.
def strategy(data):
    return data["close"] < 0

modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

An order does not itself change owned inventory. Accepted orders reserve resources; fills change cash and holdings; cancellations release only unfilled commitments. Keep available cash distinct from settled or total ledger cash. The educational lab uses immediate settlement, long-only integer shares, and one symbol, so its simplicity remains visible.

Use a stable fill ID and an atomic transaction to book cash, shares, and fill history together. Money should have an explicit precision policy. The downloadable project uses integer cents for prices and a deterministic commission rounding rule; a production adapter must match the broker's actual currency and settlement semantics.

$$
E_t=C_t+q_tP_{mark,t}
$$

## A worked example

Harbor starts with $10,000. Buying 40 shares at $100 with a $2 fee leaves $5,998 cash and 40 shares. Marking at $101 produces equity of $10,038: $5,998 plus $4,040. The $38 gain combines $40 unrealized appreciation with the $2 entry fee.

A pending order for 60 additional shares is not a holding. It reserves buying power using its price cap and a fee buffer. Canceling that remainder releases the reserve without undoing the 40-share fill.

## Implementation and review

Test cash and share conservation after every transition, not just at the final report. Reconcile independent order and fill records after restart. Compare paper outcomes with the documented simulation model; vendor paper environments can differ from live conditions, and the offline lab does not model queue position, market impact, borrow, or settlement delays. Treat correct arithmetic as evidence of ledger correctness, not a forecast of execution quality.

modules.title: Position sizing and circuit breakers
modules.subtitle: Translate uncertain return assumptions into constrained position sizes and explicit loss-control states.
modules.objective: Translate uncertain return assumptions into constrained position sizes and explicit loss-control states.
modules.reading: Unit 4 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Kelly sizing maximizes expected log growth in a specified repeated-bet model; it does not supply reliable probabilities or eliminate drawdowns. The binary-bet expression assumes a known win probability, a fixed payoff ratio, and losses bounded by the staked fraction. Stock gaps, changing payoffs, correlated bets, and estimation error break a literal mapping.

Fractional Kelly reduces the output of that model, but remains sensitive to its inputs. Practical sizing also needs capital, exposure, liquidity, and loss limits. A stop distance is a planned trigger distance, not a guaranteed maximum loss: a gap or unavailable market can execute beyond it.

$$
f^*=p-(1-p)/b;\quad q_{risk}=\lfloor B/|P_{entry}-P_{stop}|\rfloor
$$

## A worked example

For a hypothetical even-money bet with win probability 0.55, full Kelly is 0.55−0.45 = 10%; half Kelly is 5%. If the true probability is 0.51, full Kelly is only 2%. The original estimate therefore matters more than the apparent precision of the arithmetic.

Under a separate stop-risk rule, a $200 loss budget and $2 distance suggest 100 shares before other caps. If an entry gaps from a $50 assumption to $55 while the stop remains $48, the $7 distance suggests at most 28 integer shares. Recompute at the executable price.

## Implementation and review

Keep the position-size function deterministic and place it after the model proposal. Validate positive distances and finite inputs before division. Combine the resulting cap with cash, single-name, and portfolio constraints. Define which events halt new risk and who can resume. A halt blocks new exposure; cancellation and risk reduction require their own reconciled procedures.

# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.

modules.title: Portfolio exposure and outstanding commitments
modules.subtitle: Aggregate correlated positions and open-order commitments before approving a new trade.
modules.objective: Aggregate correlated positions and open-order commitments before approving a new trade.
modules.reading: Unit 4 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A collection of individually acceptable orders can violate the account's overall limits. Calculate projected cash and holdings after outstanding commitments, then test gross exposure, net exposure, single-name concentration, sector concentration, and any factor budgets supported by reliable estimates. Different measures detect different failure modes.

For a long-only account, net and gross dollar exposure coincide, but sector and name concentration still differ. A future long/short extension cannot assume that netting removes liquidity or margin risk. An exposure estimate also needs a declared mark and stale-price policy.

$$
w_{projected}=(N_{held}+N_{pending}+N_{new})/E
$$

## A worked example

Harbor's $100,000 account holds $12,000 in one name and has an accepted $5,000 buy outstanding. A proposed additional $4,000 would produce $21,000 projected exposure. It breaches a stipulated 20% name limit even though the current holding is only 12%. The maximum extra notional under this cap is $3,000 before fee and price buffers.

Two $10,000 positions in different companies may still create $20,000 exposure to the same industry. Splitting orders across names does not necessarily diversify the underlying economic risk.

## Implementation and review

Recompute reservations atomically with acceptance, so two simultaneous proposals cannot both consume the same remaining budget. Revalue after material price changes; a limit that held at submission can be exceeded by the market without any new order. Such a breach should trigger the declared review or reduction policy, not rewrite historical acceptance records. Test concurrent buys, opposite-side commitments, and a stale mark.

modules.title: Pre-trade gates and invariants
modules.subtitle: Make invalid prices, stale data, unavailable cash, and policy breaches fail before order acceptance.
modules.objective: Make invalid prices, stale data, unavailable cash, and policy breaches fail before order acceptance.
modules.reading: Unit 4 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A risk gate evaluates a typed proposal against a consistent account and market snapshot. Validate the schema first: known instrument, supported side, positive integer quantity, finite positive price, and an allowed order type. Then validate freshness and session eligibility, followed by cash, shares, exposure, and halt policy. A malformed number must never participate in arithmetic as if it were valid.

Collect explicit rejection reasons rather than replacing invalid input with zero. The exact evaluation order is an implementation choice, but every mandatory condition must hold. Keep model confidence outside this permission boundary: confidence can influence a proposed target, while the gate owns hard limits.

$$
qP_{cap}+Fee(q,P_{cap})\leq C_{available}
$$

## A worked example

Available cash is $1,000, a buy price cap is $100, and commission is 10 bps. Ten shares require $1,001, so the order fails cash validation. Nine require $900.90 and fit that constraint. They still need to pass all other gates.

A quote can have an acceptable price and insufficient freshness. An order can fit the name limit and exceed the sector limit. Passing one gate is not a general approval.

## Implementation and review

Write assertions over all accepted orders: projected cash never becomes negative under the fill-price cap; cumulative fills never exceed authorized quantity; sell reservations never exceed owned shares. Mutate one input at a time to test each rejection. The lab's market-event flag and price cap are explicit simplifications, with no exchange calendar or broker connection. Keep an invariant failure visible and halt further mutations until the state is reconciled.

modules.title: Halts, loss limits, and controlled resumption
modules.subtitle: Design a persistent operating-state machine that separates stopping new risk from managing existing exposure.
modules.objective: Design a persistent operating-state machine that separates stopping new risk from managing existing exposure.
modules.reading: Unit 4 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Define states such as running, new-risk halted, reconciling, and disabled. A loss threshold, stale feed, ledger mismatch, or unknown external order may require different actions, but each transition needs a recorded reason. A halt must survive restart; otherwise reboot becomes an accidental permission reset.

Stopping new risk does not guarantee that all orders disappeared or that positions are flat. Cancel outstanding entries through the order manager and reconcile their actual results. A reduction order still needs valid quantity, price, session, and execution controls; an emergency label is not a license to corrupt the ledger.

$$
L_{session}=1-E_t/E_{start}
$$

## A worked example

A session begins with equity $100,000 and later marks at $97,400. The session loss is 2.6%, crossing Harbor's illustrative 2.5% halt threshold. Peak-to-trough drawdown would use a different denominator if equity had first risen above $100,000. Decide which measure the policy means.

If equity rebounds to $98,000, a latched halt remains active until an explicit review and resume event. Automatic oscillation around the boundary can produce repeated stop-and-start trading.

## Implementation and review

Write a resumption checklist tied to evidence: current balances reconcile, unknown orders are resolved, input freshness is restored, the triggering defect is understood, and a permitted reviewer records the release. Test restart while halted, a fill arriving during the halt, and an attempted unreviewed resume. The educational project offers an explicit resume method for experiments; it is not a multi-user approval system.

modules.title: Labels, overlapping horizons, and time splits
modules.subtitle: Construct prediction targets without allowing future labels or fitted preprocessing to leak into evaluation.
modules.objective: Construct prediction targets without allowing future labels or fitted preprocessing to leak into evaluation.
modules.reading: Unit 5 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A label has an observation time and an end time: a five-day forward return becomes fully known five days later. Features at a decision time must use only information available then. Training rows whose labels extend into the evaluation interval can carry future information across an apparently chronological boundary.

Use forward validation with a training cutoff that respects label availability. Purge overlapping label intervals when necessary. A fixed gap in a time-series splitter is convenient for fixed horizons, but it does not automatically identify variable event horizons or solve every dependence problem. An embargo is a separate exclusion interval; naming a split purged does not make it so.

$$
\text{Eligible training row }i:\quad t^{label}_{end,i}<t^{validation}_{start}
$$

## A worked example

Validation begins at time index 10. Candidate training labels begin at 4, 6, and 8 and end three steps later at 7, 9, and 11. Under a strict end-before-validation rule, the first two are eligible; the row ending at 11 is excluded. Training data that starts before 10 can still contain a label unavailable at 10.

A scaler is fitted on the eligible training features and then applied unchanged to validation. Fitting it on all dates leaks information even if the labels were properly separated.

## Implementation and review

Save train, validation, and test index manifests with label intervals and data versions. Unit-test boundary cases where a label ends exactly at the cutoff and explicitly declare whether that endpoint is allowed. Tune only on development folds and retain a later frozen evaluation. Report the number of independent time periods, not just the number of overlapping rows.

assignment.prompt: Validation starts at 20. Label ends are 17, 19, 20, and 23. Apply the strict rule and explain why a generic random split is unsuitable here.
assignment.solution: Only 17 and 19 qualify. The strict rule excludes the endpoint at 20. A random split can train on future outcomes and overlapping intervals relative to an earlier evaluation decision.

exercise.question: A training feature is dated 8 but its forward label ends at 11; validation starts at 10. Under the strict rule it is:
exercise.explanation: The outcome was not complete before validation began.

exercises.explanation: A fixed number of rows need not cover variable endpoint overlap.

modules.title: Baselines and prediction-to-position mapping
modules.subtitle: Compare simple predictive baselines and convert model output into a bounded decision under trading costs.
modules.objective: Compare simple predictive baselines and convert model output into a bounded decision under trading costs.
modules.reading: Unit 5 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Start with an explicit no-skill baseline: a training mean for regression or a training base rate for classification. A complex model must improve a relevant out-of-sample objective, not merely fit the training data. Compare squared error, calibration where relevant, ranking quality, and eventual cost-aware decisions without conflating them.

A prediction in return units can be compared with estimated trading costs. A rank cannot directly be treated as a return magnitude, and a probability of a positive return does not state the size of wins or losses. Define the mapping from model output to target before evaluating the holdout.

$$
MSE=n^{-1}\sum_i(y_i-\hat y_i)^2
$$

## A worked example

Observed validation returns are 1% and −1%. The zero-return baseline has mean squared error 0.0001. Predictions of 0.8% and −0.6% have MSE 0.00001, improving this tiny illustrative sample. Two rows are insufficient evidence of durable performance.

If a proposed trade has expected benefit 8 bps and estimated nonoverlapping cost 6 bps, only 2 bps remain before model uncertainty. Harbor may require an additional margin or abstain. Position size is capped by deterministic risk logic even if the prediction is large.

## Implementation and review

Log the baseline, prediction units, evaluation dates, costs, turnover, and target mapping. Inspect whether apparent gains come from one outlier or one regime. A ranking model may be assessed with cross-sectional rank correlation, but time-series dependence and universe construction still affect inference. Keep predictive evaluation and portfolio simulation as separate evidence artifacts.

predicted = [0.008, -0.006]

for i in range(2):

print("Model MSE:", error / 2)
print("Zero baseline MSE:", 0.0001)

modules.title: Boosted trees and defensible constraints
modules.subtitle: Develop a nonlinear model with controlled complexity, time-aware selection, and documented feature assumptions.
modules.objective: Develop a nonlinear model with controlled complexity, time-aware selection, and documented feature assumptions.
modules.reading: Unit 5 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Boosting adds learners that correct the current model under a specified loss. Depth, learning rate, number of rounds, minimum leaf support, and regularization influence complexity. More rounds can improve training loss while degrading later performance. Use a chronologically valid validation set for early stopping and preserve the chosen iteration with the model artifact.

A monotonic constraint imposes a direction on a model's response to a selected feature while other inputs are held fixed. It expresses a modeling assumption. It does not prove that a financial relationship is universally monotonic, causal, or stable across regimes. Forcing an unjustified relationship can reduce accuracy.

$$
m^*=\arg\min_m L_{validation}(m)
$$

## A worked example

Validation losses over five training checkpoints are 0.90, 0.75, 0.71, 0.73, and 0.78. Under this illustrative selection rule, checkpoint three is preferred. Choosing checkpoint five merely because it trained longest ignores the validation evidence. The final test set must not become another tuning input.

Harbor considers a positive constraint on a quality score. Before adopting it, the team documents the score's definition, tests an unconstrained baseline, and checks whether the same feature meaning survives revisions. A renamed or rescaled feature is not automatically compatible with an old constraint vector.

## Implementation and review

The in-app worksheet illustrates model selection arithmetic; it does not train XGBoost. For an optional external extension, pin a supported library version, save feature order and constraints, inspect that version's early-stopping prediction behavior, and reproduce the result from a clean environment. Report the validation manifest and rejected variants. The later standard-library project trains a small ridge model to make the fit/evaluate boundary runnable without extra dependencies.

print("Selected loss:", losses[best])

modules.title: Calibration, thresholds, and drift
modules.subtitle: Evaluate probability quality and monitor changes in data, predictions, and delayed outcomes.
modules.objective: Evaluate probability quality and monitor changes in data, predictions, and delayed outcomes.
modules.reading: Unit 5 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Calibration asks whether predicted probabilities agree with observed frequencies in comparable cases. Discrimination asks whether the model separates outcomes. A proper score such as Brier loss reflects more than calibration alone, so a lower score is not a pure proof of better calibration. Inspect reliability bins with counts and uncertainty as well as aggregate scores.

Fit a calibration transform using development data separate from the base model's fitting observations, under a valid time design. Never calibrate on the final holdout and then report that same holdout as untouched. A calibrated probability still needs a payoff and cost model before becoming a trading decision.

$$
BS=n^{-1}\sum_i(p_i-y_i)^2
$$

## A worked example

Predictions 0.8 and 0.3 face outcomes 1 and 0. The Brier score is ((0.8−1)² + (0.3−0)²)/2 = 0.065. A constant 0.5 forecast scores 0.25 on these two observations. This is an arithmetic comparison, not enough data to establish calibration.

If a winning trade gains 1 unit and a losing trade loses 1, expected gross payoff is 2p−1. With a cost of 0.1 units per trade, break-even requires p above 0.55 under those stipulated payoffs. Different loss sizes change the threshold.

## Implementation and review

Monitor feature missingness, schema changes, prediction distribution, abstention frequency, and eventually realized label quality. Covariate drift does not necessarily imply performance failure; stable inputs do not prove stable outcomes either. Outcomes arrive late, so distinguish immediate operational alerts from delayed predictive monitoring. A drift alert should trigger a declared review or fallback; it should not silently retrain and promote a model.

print("Symmetric payoff threshold:", (1 + 0.1) / 2)

# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.

modules.title: AI decision layers and authority boundaries
modules.subtitle: Assign useful research tasks to AI while keeping order permissions and risk limits outside model-generated text.
modules.objective: Assign useful research tasks to AI while keeping order permissions and risk limits outside model-generated text.
modules.reading: Unit 6 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

An AI component can summarize evidence, extract candidate facts, classify documents, or draft a research rationale. A deterministic controller validates these outputs and decides whether they are usable. Separate a research recommendation from an authorized target, and keep both separate from broker submission.

A multi-agent committee can provide different analytical perspectives, but agreement is not independence when agents share the same model, prompt, or source error. More discussion does not convert missing evidence into a fact. Start with a small bounded workflow and add autonomous steps only when their benefit can be evaluated.

$$
q_{accepted}=RiskGate(Proposal,Account,Market,Policy)
$$

## A worked example

An AI analyst proposes a 30% position with a confidence score of 0.9. Harbor's fixed single-name cap is 10%. The proposal is rejected or resized under the declared deterministic policy. The model's explanation cannot override the cap, and confidence is not an authenticated permission.

A second proposal includes a plausible conclusion but no source identifier for its revenue figure. The research controller marks the required evidence missing and abstains. Passing numeric risk checks does not repair an unsupported premise.

## Implementation and review

Define a narrow input/output contract: task, document identifiers, allowed fields, uncertainty or missing status, and an explanation linked to evidence. Keep API secrets and trading tools out of document-analysis context. Evaluate correctness, unsupported claims, abstentions, latency, and cost against a deterministic or human-reviewed baseline. The downloadable AI lab uses fixed fictional responses to test validation; it does not call an AI provider or imply measured model accuracy.

modules.title: Filing retrieval and evidence records
modules.subtitle: Build a point-in-time research packet that preserves document identity, reporting units, and claim provenance.
modules.objective: Build a point-in-time research packet that preserves document identity, reporting units, and claim provenance.
modules.reading: Unit 6 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Retrieval selects candidate evidence; generation interprets it. Store each document's issuer, filing type, reporting period, publication timestamp, revision identity, and retrieval provenance. A semantic match does not establish that a passage answers the question or was available at a historical decision time.

Chunk boundaries should retain headings and table context. A revenue number without currency, scale, period, or scope can be materially misleading. Keep the original document pointer and local source identifier so a reviewer can trace the candidate fact. Access and redistribution rights for stored documents remain separate from their usefulness as evidence.

$$
Value_{base}=Value_{reported}\times UnitMultiplier
$$

## A worked example

A fictional Harbor filing published on March 15 reports prior-year revenue of 120 million currency units. It is eligible for an April 1 research decision but not a March 1 historical decision. An amended filing published April 20 cannot silently replace it in the April 1 record.

The analyst extracts 120 and tags the unit as millions. A controller normalizes it to 120,000,000 for a ratio calculation. If the accompanying text said thousands, the same digits would mean a thousandfold smaller amount. Preserve both the reported and normalized value.

## Implementation and review

Test missing pages, conflicting revisions, ambiguous table headers, and a relevant-looking passage about the wrong issuer. Require an explicit not-found outcome. An evidence packet should include the question, allowed as-of time, candidate documents, supported fields, unresolved disagreements, and reviewer disposition. A citation points to a source; it does not prove that the generated claim follows from it.

modules.title: Structured extraction and numeric validation
modules.subtitle: Validate AI-extracted facts beyond JSON syntax by checking provenance, units, scope, and arithmetic.
modules.objective: Validate AI-extracted facts beyond JSON syntax by checking provenance, units, scope, and arithmetic.
modules.reading: Unit 6 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A schema can require fields and restrict types; it cannot guarantee that a value is true. Validate source membership, instrument identity, reporting period, allowed units, numeric finiteness, and consistency with the supplied evidence. Reject unknown fields when they could be interpreted as instructions or unauthorized actions.

Keep reported facts separate from derived ratios and judgment. Let deterministic code compute ratios from validated inputs, with explicit zero-denominator and missing-value behavior. Avoid using a generated ratio when the underlying numerator and denominator are available for verification.

$$
g=Revenue_{current}/Revenue_{prior}-1
$$

## A worked example

A fictional evidence record states current revenue 120 million and prior revenue 100 million. The computed growth is 20%. A generated response of 200% has valid numeric syntax but fails arithmetic reconciliation. A response saying 120 thousand fails its unit contract even though its raw number matches.

If prior revenue is zero, percentage growth under this formula is undefined. The controller should return a missing or not-applicable result with a reason instead of producing an infinite score that might dominate position sizing.

## Implementation and review

Build accepted and rejected fixtures before connecting a provider. Include a fabricated source ID, mixed currencies, a future filing, an omitted field, a zero denominator, and unsupported instructions embedded in a note. Measure false acceptance as well as extraction completeness. The offline fixture project demonstrates strict comparison against supplied records; general document interpretation still requires a separately evaluated extraction system.

modules.title: Agent tools, prompt injection, and evaluation
modules.subtitle: Keep untrusted retrieved text from changing tool permissions and test bounded AI workflows against adversarial fixtures.
modules.objective: Keep untrusted retrieved text from changing tool permissions and test bounded AI workflows against adversarial fixtures.
modules.reading: Unit 6 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A retrieved filing, webpage, tool response, or agent message is data, even when it contains imperative language. A passage that says ignore the risk policy does not acquire authority because it appears in a source document. Enforce allowed operations in application code, with narrow tool arguments and task-scoped permissions.

Use a bounded workflow: retrieve approved documents, extract candidate facts, validate evidence, draft a memo, and submit for review. Set maximum calls, elapsed time, and output size. A recursive agent loop without a budget can fail operationally even if every individual response is harmless. Secrets and broker capabilities do not belong in a read-only research worker.

$$
Cost_{budget}=N_{calls,max}\times Cost_{call,assumed}
$$

## A worked example

Harbor budgets four analysis calls at an illustrative $0.03 each, for $0.12 maximum modeled call cost. A fifth requested call is stopped by the controller. An embedded source instruction requesting a cash transfer is recorded as untrusted content and has no corresponding allowed tool.

The evaluation suite includes supported extraction, missing evidence, fabricated citations, conflicting filings, prompt injection, malformed output, and provider timeout. Score whether the workflow produces the expected decision and evidence, not whether its prose sounds confident.

## Implementation and review

Test defenses outside the prompt: reject disallowed tool names, constrain schemas, preserve a permission boundary, and verify that rejected requests create no state changes. Prompt instructions can help the model behave but are not an access-control mechanism. A timeout should lead to a declared fallback or abstention, never a stale recommendation promoted as fresh. Track false acceptance, unsupported claims, correct abstention, latency, and cost separately.

modules.title: Async queues, backpressure, and retry budgets
modules.subtitle: Prevent slow consumers and ambiguous writes from turning transient failures into duplicated work or stale decisions.
modules.objective: Prevent slow consumers and ambiguous writes from turning transient failures into duplicated work or stale decisions.
modules.reading: Unit 7 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

An asynchronous pipeline needs bounded queues and an overload policy. Waiting for queue capacity creates backpressure; dropping or coalescing observations is a separate policy that may be appropriate for some quote updates but not for authoritative fills. A queue is not a durable ledger, and process-local async coordination does not automatically coordinate threads or machines.

Classify operations before retrying. Repeating a read is different from resubmitting an order whose outcome is unknown. Bound attempts, use a total deadline, and apply jitter where appropriate to avoid synchronized retries. Reconcile an ambiguous write before deciding whether it can be repeated.

$$
t_{full}=Capacity_{free}/(Rate_{in}-Rate_{out})
$$

## A worked example

A consumer handles 80 events per second while a producer supplies 100. Backlog grows by 20 per second. A queue with 200 free slots fills in roughly 10 seconds under those constant rates. An unlimited queue hides the overload in rising latency and memory use.

A sequence of retry delays 1, 2, and 4 seconds consumes seven seconds before considering request duration. If the decision expires after five seconds, the planned retry schedule is already inconsistent with its freshness budget.

## Implementation and review

Measure queue depth and age of the oldest event, not just CPU use. Define priority and preservation rules for fills, cancellations, and observations. Use structured shutdown: stop new proposals, drain or persist authoritative events, reconcile orders, and close resources. The synchronous offline lab isolates accounting first; an async extension must preserve the same invariants across task cancellation and process failure.

modules.title: Durable state and crash recovery
modules.subtitle: Use transactions and stable identities to reconstruct orders, fills, and risk state after interruption.
modules.objective: Use transactions and stable identities to reconstruct orders, fills, and risk state after interruption.
modules.reading: Unit 7 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Persist the decision identity, immutable order payload, fills, and risk-state transitions. A uniqueness constraint prevents the same identity from creating multiple local records; a payload comparison detects a conflicting reuse of that identity. Merely returning the old result for a changed payload hides a caller defect.

An atomic transaction should encompass all local ledger changes caused by a fill. If the process stops midway, recovery sees either the committed fill and its effects or neither. This does not create an atomic transaction with an external broker: network submission still needs an intent record, stable external identifiers, and reconciliation.

$$
State_{recovered}=Fold(State_0,UniqueCommittedFills)
$$

## A worked example

Fill F1 buys 10 shares for $1,000 plus a $1 fee. Applying it twice under the same unchanged fill identity must leave one ledger entry, a $1,001 cash reduction, and 10 shares. Reusing F1 for 12 shares is a conflict, not another fill.

After a restart, the bot reads its persisted halt state before accepting a proposal. Reconstructing current holdings from durable fills provides an independent check against the cached account row. A disagreement blocks further trading until investigated.

## Implementation and review

Test a restart after order acceptance, after a partial fill, and while halted. Include transaction rollback and duplicate delivery fixtures. Keep schema migrations and model versions explicit. The downloadable SQLite lab uses local transactions and uniqueness, and demonstrates reopening the same database; it does not claim exactly-once execution across an external service boundary.

modules.subtitle: Instrument decision traces and operational invariants so incidents can be detected and reconstructed.

modules.reading: Unit 7 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Link market event, feature version, model version, intent, order, fill, and account update through stable correlation identifiers. Record decision reasons and timings while keeping secrets out of logs. A profit dashboard cannot explain whether a missing trade arose from absent data, an abstention, a risk rejection, or an order failure.

Separate operational measures from investment outcomes. Track data age, queue delay, rejected proposals, unknown orders, reconciliation mismatches, duplicate messages, fill latency, fees, and exposure. Performance measures require their own benchmark and horizon. A low error count can hide a component that stopped producing useful work.

$$
AcceptanceRate=N_{accepted}/N_{proposed}
$$

## A worked example

During a window with 200 proposals, 30 are rejected for stale data, 10 for risk caps, and 160 are accepted. The acceptance rate is 80%. That number alone does not tell whether the rejection policy is correct; review samples and expected fixture outcomes.

If accepted order count continues rising but no acknowledgements arrive, investigate the external-state gap rather than simply increasing retries. Unknown-order age is a more useful alert than another aggregate request-success percentage.

## Implementation and review

Write a runbook with detection signal, immediate containment, evidence to preserve, reconciliation steps, and resumption criteria. Test it using a deliberate feed outage and a duplicate fill. Version configuration and deployment artifacts so the incident can be replayed. Access to logs, backups, and secrets should follow the actual operational roles; never paste a live token into a research notebook or a course exercise.

print("Acceptance rate:", 160 / 200)
print("Stale rejection rate:", 30 / 200)

# This worksheet computes the case above. The price sandbox stays in cash.
# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.
def strategy(data):
    return data["close"] < 0

assignment.solution: Halt new risk under policy; retain intent IDs, broker lookup results, and recent fills/account snapshots. Resume only after ambiguous orders and balances reconcile and the communication cause is understood.

modules.title: Paper release gates and rollback
modules.subtitle: Build an evidence-based promotion packet and practice rollback without confusing paper results with live readiness.
modules.objective: Build an evidence-based promotion packet and practice rollback without confusing paper results with live readiness.
modules.reading: Unit 7 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

A release gate is a declared acceptance condition with supporting evidence. Examples include passing ledger invariants, reproducing a frozen replay, reconciling partial fills after restart, and rejecting malformed or stale proposals. A paper profit threshold alone does not test operational correctness.

Freeze the code, configuration, feature schema, model artifact, data version, and validation manifest together. Shadow evaluation can compare proposed decisions without executing them, while a paper canary tests a limited scope in a simulated environment. Neither automatically authorizes live deployment or demonstrates realistic liquidity.

$$
ReleaseEligible=\bigwedge_{j=1}^{k}Gate_j
$$

## A worked example

Harbor defines five mandatory gates: deterministic replay, correct fees and inventory, duplicate handling, persistent halt, and evidence-validation failures. A release passes four but fails persistent halt after restart. Its status is blocked under the declared policy even if the simulated return is positive.

Rollback restores a known software and model version, but it does not reverse fills that actually occurred. The restored process must reconcile current account state before resuming. Database schema compatibility is part of the rollback plan.

## Implementation and review

Prepare a release record with artifact hashes, test results, known limitations, an owner, and rollback instructions. Run an incident rehearsal before promotion. Keep the paper evaluation scope and capital limits visible. Any later real broker integration requires its own adapter tests, access configuration, market-data permissions, and review; this course ends at an offline educational acceptance packet.

gates = [True, True, True, False, True]
passed = 0
for gate in gates:
    if gate:
        passed = passed + 1
print("Gates passed:", passed)
print("Release eligible:", passed == len(gates))

# This worksheet computes the case above. The price sandbox stays in cash.
# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.
def strategy(data):
    return data["close"] < 0

modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

Download the [offline Python lab](/course-assets/stock-bots/paper_bot_lab.py) and its [project guide](/course-assets/stock-bots/README.md). Run it locally with Python 3.10 or later; it uses only the standard library and makes no network calls. The in-app worksheet below checks arithmetic, while the downloaded program runs the event and SQLite state machine.

The fixed rule observes completed closes 98, 99, and 100 and proposes ten shares because the last close exceeds their mean. A $100 buy limit constrains later fills. This is a deliberately tiny execution fixture, not a researched trading strategy. Policy values, synthetic events, immediate settlement, and fee rounding are declared in the project guide.

$$
E_{final}=9209.39+8(102)=10025.39
$$

## A worked example

Start with $10,000. Event E1 fills four shares at $100 with a $0.20 fee; its duplicate creates no additional fill. After closing and reopening the database, E2 fills the remaining six at $99 with a $0.30 fee. Cash is now $9,005.50 and holdings are ten shares. Replaying the first fill identity leaves both unchanged.

The lab halts new risk, reopens again, and verifies that an entry is rejected. A permitted reduction sells two shares at $102 with a $0.11 fee. Final cash is $9,209.39, shares are eight, and equity marked at $102 is $10,025.39.

## Implementation and review

Read the order, event, fill, and transition tables. Change one fixture at a time: duplicate an event, use a conflicting payload under its ID, offer a nonmarketable price, reduce volume, or cancel a remainder. Record the expected and actual state before reading the report. The toy matcher fills at the supplied event price up to eligible volume; it does not model exchange queue priority or realistic liquidity. Keep the halt active until an explicit, documented resume experiment.

# This worksheet computes the case above. The price sandbox stays in cash.

modules.title: Project: expanding-window machine learning
modules.subtitle: Fit a small ridge model in two chronological folds and compare genuinely held-out predictions with a training-only baseline.
modules.objective: Fit a small ridge model in two chronological folds and compare genuinely held-out predictions with a training-only baseline.
modules.reading: Unit 8 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

The downloaded lab's ridge_walkforward function trains a one-feature ridge regression with an unpenalized intercept. For each cutoff it computes training means, centers the observations, estimates the slope with a fixed penalty of one, and predicts only the next unseen row. No external ML dependency is required.

The artificial observations obey y=1+2x for x values −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, and 3. Units are abstract; they are not market returns. This deliberately simple fixture makes chronology and coefficient shrinkage visible. It establishes that a training and evaluation pipeline runs correctly, not that a stock model has skill.

$$
\hat\beta=\frac{\sum(x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)}{\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2+\lambda}
$$

## A worked example

The first fold trains on four rows. Centered cross-product is 10 and centered squared-feature sum is 5, so slope is 10/(5+1)=1.6667. Its intercept is 0.8333, and prediction at x=2 is 4.1667 versus actual 5. The training-mean baseline predicts zero.

The second fold trains on five rows, with slope 20/11=1.8182 and intercept 1. Its prediction at x=3 is 6.4545 versus actual 7; the training-mean baseline predicts one. Across these two held-out predictions the ridge MSE is about 0.495983, versus 30.5 for the baseline.

## Implementation and review

Inspect the saved fold rows and verify that changing the final y value cannot alter either prediction. It can change the final evaluation error, because that is the correct role of a held-out outcome. For a financial extension, replace artificial inputs only after defining point-in-time features, label intervals, costs, and a frozen target mapping. Do not tune the penalty on these two final outcomes and continue calling them untouched.
modules.code:
slope1 = 10 / 6
pred1 = slope1 * 2.5
slope2 = 20 / 11
pred2 = 1 + slope2 * 3
print("First prediction:", pred1)
print("Second prediction:", pred2)
print("Walk-forward MSE:", ((pred1 - 5) ** 2 + (pred2 - 7) ** 2) / 2)
print("Baseline MSE:", (5 ** 2 + 6 ** 2) / 2)

# This worksheet computes the case above. The price sandbox stays in cash.
# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.
def strategy(data):
    return data["close"] < 0

assignment.prompt: Reproduce both fold predictions. Then change only the last outcome from 7 to 8 and explain which fitted quantities must remain unchanged.
assignment.solution: Both fitted slopes and predictions stay unchanged because the last outcome is not used for training either fold. The second prediction's error and aggregate MSE change. Earlier observed outcomes may legitimately enter later expanding training windows.

modules.title: Project: a verifiable AI research packet
modules.subtitle: Test a deterministic evidence validator with accepted, fabricated, unavailable, and malformed model-response fixtures.
modules.objective: Test a deterministic evidence validator with accepted, fabricated, unavailable, and malformed model-response fixtures.
modules.reading: Unit 8 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

The downloaded validate_fact function evaluates a fixed candidate response against a supplied fictional evidence record. It requires an exact field set, known source, matching issuer and period, allowed unit, finite numeric value, and an as-of date after availability. It then computes growth from the verified source values.

This is the validation half of an AI research workflow. The project does not call a language model or retrieve real filings. Fixed response fixtures make false acceptance testable without provider credentials. A later model integration would need its own extraction-quality evaluation and document access policy.

$$
VerifiedGrowth=120/100-1=0.20
$$

## A worked example

Source HBR-2025-v1 is available at fixture time 15 and records revenue 120 and prior revenue 100 in USD millions. The candidate passes at time 20 and produces 20% growth. It fails at time 10 because the evidence is not yet available. Changing the source ID, value, unit, issuer, or period causes rejection.

Adding an unexpected execute_order field also fails the strict schema. The research validator has no broker tool. This illustrates an enforced boundary whose outcome can be inspected in code and state, rather than relying on a generated promise to obey instructions.

## Implementation and review

Create a labeled evaluation table before connecting a provider: supported fact, unknown source, wrong scale, future record, nonfinite number, extra instruction, and missing required field. Count correct acceptances and correct abstentions separately. Avoid making the validator permissive just to improve apparent completion rate. Keep the verified record and the source pointer together when writing the final research memo.

print("Verified growth:", 120 / 100 - 1)
print("Source eligible at time 10:", 15 <= 10)
print("Source eligible at time 20:", 15 <= 20)

# Its equity curve is not evidence for the bot or model's performance.

modules.objective: Integrate the strategy contract, replay ledger, ML evaluation, AI evidence tests, and operational review into one defensible release packet.
modules.reading: Unit 8 engineering study. Produce the assignment artifact, reproduce the worksheet, and consult the primary references below. All Harbor cases are fictional.
modules.content:
## Design and reasoning

The final deliverable is a reproducible educational system and a written decision about its tested scope. Assemble the decision contract from Unit 1, rule and cost specification from Unit 2, order transition table from Unit 3, risk gates from Unit 4, split manifest from Unit 5, evidence-validation matrix from Unit 6, and incident runbook from Unit 7.

Run the downloadable project from a clean environment and retain the code revision, fixture inputs, output, and assumptions. The paper rule, artificial ridge experiment, and fixed AI response tests are distinct experiments in one packet. Do not imply that the ridge or AI fixture has been validated as a live trading signal.

$$
Score=15+25+20+15+15+10=100
$$

## A worked example

The default paper replay reconciles to $10,025.39 equity, three fills, $0.61 fees, and an active halt. The artificial ridge comparison yields MSE about 0.495983 versus 30.5 for its baseline. The evidence validator accepts the supported 120-million revenue record and derives 20% growth. Each result answers a different acceptance question.

Suppose an altered implementation reports the same final equity but creates two fills for E1 and later offsets them. The final number matches while event idempotency fails. Review both state invariants and the full transition trace; a favorable final balance cannot excuse invalid intermediate actions.

## Implementation and review

Use a 100-point self-assessment: decision and data contract 15, execution and ledger evidence 25, risk and restart behavior 20, ML evaluation 15, AI evidence and permissions 15, and incident/release documentation 10. Require at least 80 points and no unresolved failure of cash/share conservation, duplicate handling, persistent halts, or source validation. The automatic final exam assesses conceptual transfer; it does not grade the code or written dossier. Conclude what the tests support, what remains simulated, and what experiment would challenge the weakest assumption next.

prerequisites: Comfort with Python functions, lists, and basic probability. Complete Trading & market fundamentals and the strategy-evaluation units in Quantitative Investment Analysis first. The offline project requires Python 3.10+; no credentials or paid services are needed.
outcomes: Specify point-in-time signals and reproducible evaluation contracts.
Reconcile targets, pending orders, partial fills, cash, and inventory.
Enforce deterministic sizing, exposure, freshness, and halt policies.
Fit and evaluate a small chronological ML model without test leakage.
Validate AI evidence and constrain tools outside generated text.
Produce a replayable paper-bot project and an incident acceptance dossier.
readingGuide: Eight units, 32 original lessons, 64 practice questions, seven checkpoints, and a 32-question final. Complete the worksheet and written artifact in each lesson. The final unit includes a downloadable standard-library paper bot, an actual small ridge fit, and fixed AI response validation tests. These are offline educational projects, with explicit simulation assumptions; the written capstone is self-assessed separately from the automatic exam.

questions.explanation: All independent limits must hold, so use the smaller quantity.

A proposed quantity is negative but its absolute notional fits the budget. The gate should:
options: Turn it into a buy silently
questions.explanation: Side and positive quantity are separate validated fields.

questions.question: Equity starts at $40,000 and falls to $38,800. Session loss is:
Validation starts at 30 and label ends are 27, 29, 31. How many meet end < 30?
questions.explanation: Ends 27 and 29 qualify; 31 does not.

questions.question: A model improves MSE but trades much more often. What is still required?
options: Evaluate its fixed decision rule with costs
questions.explanation: Predictive accuracy and realized economic performance are different objectives.

questions.question: Validation losses are 0.6, 0.5, 0.52. Which checkpoint has minimum loss?
questions.explanation: The second checkpoint has loss 0.5.

questions.question: For p=0.7 and outcome 1, the individual Brier loss is:
questions.explanation: Square the forecast error: (0.7−1)² = 0.09.

questions.question: A model recommends 18% exposure under a hard 7% cap. The controller must:
options: Enforce the 7% cap or reject under policy
Accept because the prose is persuasive
Ask the model to disable the cap
questions.explanation: Authority remains in the deterministic permission and risk layer.

questions.question: A later amended filing disagrees with the version used in an earlier decision. The audit record should:
options: Preserve both versions with their availability times
questions.explanation: Point-in-time reconstruction requires the original evidence set.

questions.question: Revenue rises from 200 to 230 with consistent units. Verified growth is:
questions.explanation: Divide by the prior revenue base: 230/200−1 = 15%.

questions.question: A workflow has a three-call budget and requests a fourth. The controller should:
options: Enforce the limit and use its declared fallback
Let the model redefine the limit
questions.explanation: Resource budgets are application policy, not model suggestions.

questions.question: Free capacity 120, arrivals 90/s, service 60/s. Time to full is:
questions.explanation: Backlog grows by 30 per second; 120/(90−60) = 4 seconds.

questions.question: One unique fill buys 5 shares for $250 plus $0.25 fee from $1,000. Replaying it unchanged leaves cash:
questions.explanation: The fill is booked once: 1,000−250−0.25.

questions.question: Of 250 proposals, 50 are rejected. Acceptance rate is:
questions.explanation: There are 200 accepted proposals; 200/250 = 80%.

questions.question: A paper canary passes. The supported conclusion is:
options: Data licensing is no longer relevant
questions.explanation: Evidence is limited to the tested model and environment.

questions.question: An unchanged E1 event is replayed after its four-share fill. Expected additional shares are:
questions.explanation: Stable event and fill identities prevent duplicate booking.

questions.question: A baseline predicts 0 and 1 against outcomes 5 and 7. Its MSE is:
A source becomes available at time 40 and the decision is at 35. The validator should:
options: Accept because it can be retrieved now
Reject it as unavailable at the decision time
questions.explanation: A valid identifier is insufficient without valid availability.

questions.question: A replay's final equity matches the expected value but intermediate cash becomes negative. The correct conclusion is:
questions.explanation: A valid final balance does not repair an invalid state transition.

modules.title: Tokenomics & monetary theory
modules.subtitle: Separate protocol activity from tokenholder value
modules.content:
## The idea

A protocol can be useful without distributing economic value to its token. Examine issuance, unlocks, fee routing, burns, governance rights, and who bears operating costs. Nominal staking yield includes compensation for dilution and risk.

$$
MV=PY
$$

## A worked example

A staking token pays 8% more units while total token supply grows 6%. A simple dilution-adjusted unit yield is 1.08/1.06 − 1, about 1.89%, before price changes, fees, slashing, and taxes. This is not a risk-free return.

## Research protocol

Read the actual economic rights and contract controls. Never treat proof-of-stake yield as literally risk-free: validator, slashing, liquidity, governance, and smart-contract risks remain.

### In the sandbox

Run the lesson template, then change one assumption at a time. Record the parameter, the observed change, and whether the result supports your original claim. All default price paths are synthetic, and the accompanying trend strategy demonstrates execution mechanics. Its returns do not validate the lesson’s valuation thesis.

exercise.question: An 8% staking yield with 6% supply growth implies approximately:
exercise.explanation: Adjust the units by total supply growth: 1.08 / 1.06 − 1.

modules.title: AMMs & impermanent loss
modules.subtitle: Derive swap output from the invariant
modules.content:
## The idea

A constant-product pool quotes trades from reserves rather than matching an order book. A large swap moves the marginal price. Trading fees change the effective input, while liquidity providers bear exposure to relative price movements.

$$
\Delta y=\frac{y\,\Delta x(1-f)}{x+\Delta x(1-f)},\qquad IL(k)=\frac{2\sqrt{k}}{1+k}-1
$$

## A worked example

A pool contains 10 ETH and 20,000 USDC. Selling 1 ETH with no fee returns 20,000/11, about 1,818.18 USDC. The average execution price is worse than the initial 2,000 USDC marginal price. If the external price doubles, full-range impermanent loss is about 5.72% relative to holding.

## Research protocol

Use the AMM simulator to vary trade size, fees, and relative price. Full-range IL omits fee income. Concentrated positions need separate piecewise inventory accounting inside and outside their price ranges.

### In the sandbox

Run the lesson template, then change one assumption at a time. Record the parameter, the observed change, and whether the result supports your original claim. All default price paths are synthetic, and the accompanying trend strategy demonstrates execution mechanics. Its returns do not validate the lesson’s valuation thesis.

exercise.question: A larger trade relative to reserves generally causes:
exercise.explanation: The reserve curve becomes less favorable as the trade moves along it.

modules.title: Crypto arbitrage & market neutrality
modules.subtitle: A hedged position still has several kinds of risk
modules.content:
## The idea

Cash-and-carry pairs a long spot position with a short derivative. Positive funding may compensate the short, but the rate can reverse. Delta neutrality does not eliminate liquidation, basis, collateral, custody, or venue risk.

$$
\mathrm{NetCarry}\approx\mathrm{Funding}-\mathrm{Borrow}-\mathrm{Fees}-\mathrm{BasisChange}
$$

## A worked example

At a constant 0.01% funding rate every eight hours, a simple annualized rate is 0.0001 × 3 × 365 = 10.95%. This assumes unchanged rates, no fees, and no compounding; it is not a forward yield guarantee.

## Research protocol

Stress collateral in a price gap, include liquidation rules, and avoid relying on transfers between venues during a crisis. Study MEV as an execution cost and protection problem; no adversarial trading is executed by this platform.

### In the sandbox

Run the lesson template, then change one assumption at a time. Record the parameter, the observed change, and whether the result supports your original claim. All default price paths are synthetic, and the accompanying trend strategy demonstrates execution mechanics. Its returns do not validate the lesson’s valuation thesis.

exercise.question: Delta neutrality removes:
exercise.explanation: Other risks remain even when spot-price sensitivity is hedged.

modules.title: Crypto execution engineering
modules.subtitle: Track nonces, confirmations, and transaction costs
modules.content:
## The idea

On-chain execution is an asynchronous state machine. A submitted transaction can remain pending, be replaced, or be removed by a reorganization. Nonces order an account’s transactions; a nonce manager must coordinate concurrent senders.

$$
\mathrm{EffectiveGasPrice}=\min(\mathrm{MaxFee},\mathrm{BaseFee}+\mathrm{PriorityFee})
$$

## A worked example

With a base fee of 20 gwei, a priority fee of 2 gwei, and a max fee of 30 gwei, the effective price is 22 gwei. If the base fee rises above the cap, the transaction cannot be included on those terms. A higher tip still cannot guarantee inclusion.

## Research protocol

Persist transaction intents before signing, reconcile receipts, and choose a confirmation policy. Keep keys outside lesson code. The local course provides simulation only and never requests a wallet seed phrase.

### In the sandbox

Run the lesson template, then change one assumption at a time. Record the parameter, the observed change, and whether the result supports your original claim. All default price paths are synthetic, and the accompanying trend strategy demonstrates execution mechanics. Its returns do not validate the lesson’s valuation thesis.

exercise.question: A priority fee guarantees next-block inclusion:
exercise.explanation: Inclusion also depends on fee caps, block capacity, ordering, and network conditions.

modules.title: Crypto stress testing
modules.subtitle: Model liquidity loss and collateral shortfalls
modules.content:
## The idea

A stress test asks what happens under an adverse scenario rather than estimating its likelihood. Model a rapid price drop, collateral haircuts, widening spreads, and the inability to rebalance. Correlations and liquidity often deteriorate together.

$$
\mathrm{HealthFactor}=\frac{\mathrm{CollateralValue}\times\mathrm{LiquidationThreshold}}{\mathrm{DebtValue}}
$$

## A worked example

Collateral worth $10,000, a liquidation threshold of 80%, and debt of $5,000 imply a health factor of 1.6. A 50% collateral-price drop lowers it to 0.8, before interest and fees, potentially triggering liquidation.

## Research protocol

Use the flash-crash scenario and evaluate the path to liquidation, not merely the final price. For LP positions compare fee income with inventory loss, gas, and execution slippage.

### In the sandbox

Run the lesson template, then change one assumption at a time. Record the parameter, the observed change, and whether the result supports your original claim. All default price paths are synthetic, and the accompanying trend strategy demonstrates execution mechanics. Its returns do not validate the lesson’s valuation thesis.

exercise.question: A health factor below one commonly indicates:
exercise.explanation: Collateral adjusted by the liquidation threshold no longer covers debt.

print("Stressed health:", collateral * (1 - crash) * threshold / debt)

exams.title: Web3 & crypto economics final exam
exams.description: Apply each module to a new scenario. Untimed and open-book; review explanations after submission and retake whenever you are ready.

questions.question: Token issuance grows while demand stays weak. Which question is most relevant to holders?
options: How dilution and actual token utility affect value capture
Whether issuance guarantees a higher price
questions.explanation: Supply mechanics and demand for economic utility matter; issuance alone does not create holder value.

questions.question: Ignoring fees, a constant-product pool receives more of token X. What happens to its token Y reserve during the swap?
options: It must rise by the same amount
It falls so the reserve product is maintained
questions.explanation: Under x·y = k, increasing x reduces y; the difference is paid out.

questions.question: A long spot / short perpetual position collects funding. Why is its return not guaranteed?
options: Funding can change and basis, financing, and liquidation risks remain
A hedge removes every operational risk
questions.explanation: Directionally offsetting legs do not remove funding, basis, collateral, counterparty, or execution risks.

questions.question: An on-chain transaction was broadcast but the receipt is missing. What should be checked before a replacement?
options: Nonce and transaction status under the chain's confirmation rules
Assume the first transaction never existed
questions.explanation: Reconcile transaction and nonce state to avoid conflicting or duplicate economic actions.

questions.question: Collateral is $8,000, liquidation threshold 0.75, and debt $5,000. After collateral falls 25%, what is the simplified health factor?
questions.explanation: Collateral becomes $6,000; $6,000 × 0.75 / $5,000 = 0.9, below one in this simplified model.
